context.pubinfo_note: From the Consilience cross-theory demo (consilience-demo.netlify.app); its results are pinned in https://github.com/Anuja-Khatri/theconsilience-engine at commit 96ba4e435bd13718d36435cc3436d938d2d1f894, results/demo/. The demo's check rules this disagreement decidable with instruments that exist today and names the shared observable both claims bear on. This is a statement about the two claim cards, not a verdict on either theory. The axis is an axis of theoretical commitment, not a quantity axis, so no margin or floor applies. The claim statements in the linked claim cards are reviewed paraphrases with page locators, not quotations.

left.statement: IIT predicts that the neural substrate of consciousness (PSC/complex) corresponds to elements with maximum intrinsic cause–effect power, locating the content-specific NCC in the neural elements of the PSC rather than in prefrontal or other regions, consistent with a posterior cortical hot zone.
left.direction: “IIT predicts that the neural substrate of consciousness (PSC/complex) corresponds to elements with maximum intrinsic cause–effect power, locating the content-specific NCC in the neural elements of the PSC rather than in prefrontal or other regions, consistent with a posterior cortical hot zone.” (t002) — expected on shared observables: regional_decoding

right.statement: The locus of conscious processing is a large-scale prefrontal-parietal (and cingulate/temporal) cortical network, not posterior sensory cortices alone.
right.direction: “The locus of conscious processing is a large-scale prefrontal-parietal (and cingulate/temporal) cortical network, not posterior sensory cortices alone.” (c003) — expected on shared observables: regional_decoding
